alt.en: A printed hymnbook page headed "82. Balm in Gilead.": one line of melody with the first verse, "How lost was my condition, Till Jesus made me whole; There is but one Physician Can cure a sin-sick soul.", then a line marked "Chorus" with the words "There's a balm in Gil-e-ad To make the wounded whole;". Verses 2 to 7 follow as text, and at the foot are the note "Sing Chorus line twice over after each verse." and the page number, 70.
alt.es: Página impresa de un himnario con el encabezado "82. Balm in Gilead.": una línea de melodía con la primera estrofa, "How lost was my condition, Till Jesus made me whole; There is but one Physician Can cure a sin-sick soul.", y después una línea marcada "Chorus" con la letra "There's a balm in Gil-e-ad To make the wounded whole;". Siguen las estrofas 2 a 7 como texto y, al pie, la nota "Sing Chorus line twice over after each verse." y el número de página, 70.

caption.en: John Newton's hymn "The good Physician" as No. 82 in Hiram Mattison's Sacred Melodies for Social Worship (New York, 1859), headed "Balm in Gilead" and given the chorus "There's a balm in Gilead To make the wounded whole", the lines the spiritual's refrain grew from.
caption.es: El himno "The good Physician" de John Newton como n.º 82 en Sacred Melodies for Social Worship de Hiram Mattison (Nueva York, 1859), con el encabezado "Balm in Gilead" y el estribillo "There's a balm in Gilead To make the wounded whole", los versos de los que nació el estribillo del espiritual.

source: Rev. H. Mattison, Sacred Melodies for Social Worship (New York: Mason Brothers, 1859), No. 82, "Balm in Gilead", p. 70
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: SCB #5859; Internet Archive sacredmelodiesfo00matt, image n73
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1859; words by John Newton (died 1807), compiler Hiram Mattison (died 1868, per the library record). PD by age in the US (before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A page of printed music headed "Balm in Gilead" in black-letter type: four systems of four-part harmony on two staves, in four sharps and 2/4 time. Under the notes are the refrain, "There is a Balm in Gil-e-ad, To make the wounded whole", and three numbered verses beginning "Some-times I feel dis-cour-aged", "Don't ev-er feel dis-cour-aged" and "If you can-not preach like Pe-ter".
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el título "Balm in Gilead" en letra gótica: cuatro sistemas de armonía a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, con cuatro sostenidos y en compás de 2/4. Bajo las notas están el estribillo, "There is a Balm in Gil-e-ad, To make the wounded whole", y tres estrofas numeradas que empiezan "Some-times I feel dis-cour-aged", "Don't ev-er feel dis-cour-aged" y "If you can-not preach like Pe-ter".

caption.en: "Balm in Gilead" on page 43 of John Wesley Work's Folk Song of the American Negro (Nashville: Press of Fisk University, 1915), which prints again the four-part setting from his brother Frederick J. Work's songbook of 1907, the spiritual's earliest known printing.
caption.es: "Balm in Gilead" en la página 43 de Folk Song of the American Negro, de John Wesley Work (Nashville: Press of Fisk University, 1915), que vuelve a imprimir el arreglo a cuatro voces del cancionero de 1907 de su hermano Frederick J. Work, la primera impresión conocida del espiritual.

source: John Wesley Work, Folk Song of the American Negro (Nashville: Press of Fisk University, 1915), "Balm in Gilead", p. 43 (the music; the running head is cropped away)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: SCC; Internet Archive folkameric00work, image n50
licenceEvidence: Published Nashville 1915; John Wesley Work died 1925 (LoC name authority n92053236, 1873-1925); the setting is Frederick J. Work's of 1907 (died 24 January 1942, Canterbury Dictionary of Hymnology); words and tune traditional. PD in the US (before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70, from 2013 at the latest). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page numbered 88, headed "Hymns of Consolation" and "There Is a Balm in Gilead", with "Transcribed from the singing of the Hampton Institute students by R. Nathaniel Dett" and the marking "Andante molto espress" at 60 beats a minute. Five systems of four-part harmony on two staves, in five sharps, carry the refrain and then, marked "Solo", the verse "Sometimes I feel discouraged, And think my work's in vain"; verses 2 and 3 are printed as text at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa con el número 88, los encabezados "Hymns of Consolation" y "There Is a Balm in Gilead", la nota "Transcribed from the singing of the Hampton Institute students by R. Nathaniel Dett" y la indicación "Andante molto espress" a 60 pulsos por minuto. Cinco sistemas de armonía a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas, con cinco sostenidos, llevan el estribillo y después, marcada "Solo", la estrofa "Sometimes I feel discouraged, And think my work's in vain"; las estrofas 2 y 3 están impresas como texto al pie.

caption.en: "There Is a Balm in Gilead" on page 88 of R. Nathaniel Dett's Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), among the "Hymns of Consolation": the page our arrangement follows, with the refrain for everyone and the verse for one voice alone.
caption.es: "There Is a Balm in Gilead" en la página 88 de Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), de R. Nathaniel Dett, entre los "Hymns of Consolation" (himnos de consuelo): la página que sigue nuestro arreglo, con el estribillo para todos y la estrofa para una sola voz.

source: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton, Va.: Hampton Institute Press, 1927), "There Is a Balm in Gilead", p. 88
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, Benson Collection of Hymnals and Hymnology (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: BV461 .R477 1927; LCCN 27010635; OCLC 1867958; Internet Archive religiousfolkson00dett, image n119
licenceEvidence: Published Hampton, Virginia, 1927: US copyright for 1927 works ended on 31 December 2022 (95 years), so PD in the US since 1 January 2023. Dett died in 1943 (library record: "Dett, R. Nathaniel, 1882-1943"), so PD in the EU and Israel (life plus 70) since 1 January 2014. Words and tune traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de una ladera cubierta de árboles bajos y redondeados y de matorrales, que sube de izquierda a derecha bajo un cielo claro y vacío.

caption.en: Oak woods in Gilead, the hill country east of the Jordan, in a detail of a photograph made between about 1900 and 1920 by the American Colony's Photo Department in Jerusalem (Library of Congress, Matson Collection): the land of the balm in Jeremiah's question.
caption.es: Bosque de robles en Galaad, la región montañosa al este del Jordán, en un detalle de una fotografía tomada aproximadamente entre 1900 y 1920 por el departamento de fotografía de la American Colony de Jerusalén (Biblioteca del Congreso, colección Matson): la tierra del bálsamo de la pregunta de Jeremías.
